svg.title: Thinking tokens as a budget line inside one agent turn
svg.desc: A hand-drawn figure. One agent turn is drawn as a band in three segments: a prompt billed as input, a wider block of adaptive thinking tokens, and the returned answer, with both of the last two billed as output and the thinking marked as the hidden cost line. Below, an effort dial runs from low through medium, high, and xhigh to max, shaded progressively, biasing how readily the model spends thinking tokens at the price of cost and latency. On the right, two panels: the next turn carries the answer plus a short distilled note, while the raw trace is dropped — not re-fed to the next turn, kept out of the cached prefix, and kept out of long-term memory. Captions state that effort is a knob on a distribution rather than a fixed allocation, and that the window must be provisioned as prompt plus expected thinking plus answer.
svg.text: Thinking tokens are a budget line
One turn: thinking sits between prompt and answer, is billed as output, and its raw trace is dropped before the next turn.
ONE AGENT TURN · consumes one context window
both billed as output · thinking is the hidden cost line
Effort dial · biases how readily the model thinks
more thinking tokens · more quality · more cost · more latency
distilled note if it earned one
not re-fed to the next turn
It is a working note, not an artefact.
Effort is a knob on a distribution, not a fixed allocation: you say how hard to try, and the model decides how hard this request is.
Provision the window as prompt plus expected thinking plus answer. Budgeting for only the answer you can see undercounts the bill.
